simple.meaning: פִּרְדָּה (pirdâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a she-mule.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פִּרְדָּה (H6506) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 1:33, with occurrences in 1 Kings.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פִּרְדָּה (H6506) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פִּרְדָּה (H6506) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פִּרְדָּה (pirdâh) / H6506 is traced through 1 Kings 1:33, 1 Kings 1:38, 1 Kings 1:44 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The king said to them, “Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.

timeline.evidenceText: The king said to them, “Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites went down and had Solomon ride on king David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and they have caused him to ride on the king’s mule.
